command:
git fetch -q --tags origin; echo -n 'refs matching v0.8.2 exactly: '; git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v0.8.2' | wc -l | tr -d ' '; echo -n 'refs matching v0.8.2rc3 exactly: '; git ls-remote --tags origin 'refs/tags/v0.8.2rc3' | wc -l | tr -d ' '; echo -n 'existing v0.8.* tags: '; git ls-remote --tags origin 'v0.8.*' | grep -v '\^{}' | awk '{print $2}' | tr '
' ' '
note: The gate is named for 0.8.0 because it was written for that checklist; what it checks here is that neither this release's tag nor the rehearsal tag about to be cut already exists. v0.8.2rc1 and v0.8.2rc2 do exist: they are rehearsal cuts the rehearsal itself stopped in the prepare phase (D-0216, amended), and nothing was uploaded to any index under either. Matched exactly, not by prefix, so a rehearsal tag cannot stand in for the release tag.
result: no ref on origin matches refs/tags/v0.8.2 or refs/tags/v0.8.2rc3, this cut's rehearsal tag; origin carries refs/tags/v0.8.0, refs/tags/v0.8.1, refs/tags/v0.8.2rc1 and refs/tags/v0.8.2rc2
